patch_description: This replaces the Kalman/RTS pipeline with a fundamentally different paradigm: a robust, adaptively-weighted Whittaker–Henderson penalized least-squares smoother. It minimizes ||W^(1/2)(y − x)||² + λ·Σ w_i·(Δ²y)² in one global solve — a discrete smoothing spline. Unlike the sequential Kalman approach, this is zero-phase by construction (no forward/backward asymmetry), has provably minimal curvature for a given data-fidelity, and directly attacks the weakest metrics: noise reduction and slope stability (the second-difference penalty is exactly a spurious-slope-change suppressor). Adaptivity comes from (1) λ calibrated from robust MAD noise/dynamics estimates, (2) iteratively reweighted residuals (asymmetric Huber weights that down-weight noise bursts while keeping genuine signal excursions), and (3) a local penalty modulation that relaxes smoothing where the underlying signal has genuine curvature (detected via a robust second difference), preserving responsiveness and reducing lag. The global banded solve is O(n) per iteration, keeping execution time comparable. Output contract (length and index alignment) is identical to the current implementation.
